abstract:
BACKGROUND: Forkhead box O3a (FOXO3a) plays important roles in tumor development; however, its expression pattern, prognostic significance, and biological function in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remain unclear.
METHODS: FOXO3a expression was evaluated in PDAC tissues and correlated with clinicopathological characteristics and patient survival. FOXO3a-overexpressing and FOXO3a-silenced PDAC cell models were established to investigate its actions on cell growth, migratory capacity, and invasiveness. The participation of the WNT/β-catenin pathway was examined using immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and rescue experiments. Xenograft models were employed to validate the impact of FOXO3a in regulating in vivo tumor growth.
RESULTS: FOXO3a expression was significantly reduced across both PDAC tissue specimens and cell lines compared with controls. Decreased FOXO3a expression was correlated with advanced tumor stage (P = 0.008), perineural invasion (P = 0.019), and distant metastatic status (P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses demonstrated that low FOXO3a expression independently predicted poor overall survival (HR = 2.068, P = 0.004). High β-catenin expression was also identified as an independent risk factor of poor patient outcome (HR = 1.827, P = 0.014). Functionally, FOXO3a overexpression inhibited PDAC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas FOXO3a depletion promoted malignant behaviors. Mechanistically, FOXO3a suppressed the WNT/β-catenin signaling by decreasing the nuclear accumulation of β-catenin, and pathway activation partially reversed FOXO3a-mediated inhibition. In vivo, FOXO3a overexpression significantly inhibited xenograft growth.
CONCLUSION: FOXO3a downregulation exhibits a significant correlation with dverse clinicopathological features and unfavorable outcome in PDAC. FOXO3a exerts tumor-suppressive effects, at least in part, by negatively regulating the WNT/β-catenin pathway and consequently holds promise as a prognostic marker and targeted therapy for PDAC.
key_points_ko: FOXO3a 낮은 발현은 췌관선암 환자의 짧은 전체생존기간을 독립적으로 예측했습니다(위험비[HR] = 2.068, P = 0.004).
높은 β-catenin 발현 역시 환자의 나쁜 예후를 나타내는 독립적 위험 요인이었습니다(HR = 1.827, P = 0.014).
FOXO3a 발현 감소는 진행된 병기(P = 0.008), 신경 주위 침윤(P = 0.019), 원격 전이 상태(P < 0.001)와 유의하게 연관되어 있었습니다.
summary_ko: 본 연구는 췌관선암(PDAC)에서 FOXO3a의 발현 양상과 예후적 가치, 생물학적 기능을 분석했습니다. 췌관선암 조직과 세포주에서 FOXO3a 발현이 유의하게 감소해 있었으며, 이는 병기 진행 및 전이와 연관이 있었습니다. FOXO3a 과발현은 WNT/β-catenin(β-카테닌) 신호전달을 억제하여 암세포의 증식과 이동, 침윤을 줄였고 동물실험에서도 종양 성장을 억제했습니다. 따라서 FOXO3a는 췌장암의 예후 예측 인자 및 치료 타깃으로서의 가능성을 보여줍니다.
title: FOXO3a suppression predicts poor prognosis and facilitates cell migration and invasion through the WNT/β-catenin pathway in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
title_ko: 췌관선암에서 FOXO3a 억제의 예후 불량 예측 및 WNT/β-카테닌 경로를 통한 세포 이동과 침윤 촉진 효과
